items.title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT<sub>2A</sub>R–β-arrestin signaling
items.author: Sheng Wang
items.content: This study shows that the sustained antidepressant-like effect of psychedelics is driven by 5-HT2A receptor–β-arrestin signaling. Repeated low-dose LSD preserves this effect in mice without inducing hallucinogenic-like behaviors in mice or monkeys.

items.title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles
items.author: David R. Walt
items.content: The authors developed methods to identify extracellular vesicles (EVs) in the blood that come from the brain by capturing EV surface proteins. This could be used in the future to diagnose neurological diseases.

items.title: Behavioral genomics identifies Creld1 as a cross-modal regulator of somatosensation
items.author: Bailong Xiao
items.content: Jiang et al. developed a robust postnatal knockout platform for somatosensory genomics and behavioral screening, identifying Creld1 as a cross-modal regulator of somatosensation through its control of sensory neuron excitability via voltage-gated sodium channels.

items.title: Network geometry shapes the transformation of task representations across the human cortex
items.author: Michael W. Cole
items.content: The dimensionality of intrinsic brain connectivity systematically shapes how task representations compress and expand across the cortex, and activity flow modeling shows the active role of network geometry in generating the transformation.

items.title: SIK3 controls synaptic localization of NMDA receptors by phosphorylating GluN1
items.author: Thomas C. Südhof
items.content: SIK3 kinase controls synaptic NMDA receptor recruitment by phosphorylating GluN1 at a single site. Loss or inhibition of SIK3 markedly reduces synaptic NMDARs, while a gain-of-function mutation increases GluN1 phosphorylation and NMDAR levels.

items.title: A corticohypothalamic circuit that mediates maternal awakening to pup cries
items.author: Feixue Liang
items.content: Tang, Wu et al. identify a brain circuit that enables mother mice to wake selectively to pup cries. Motherhood strengthens this pathway through increased dopamine receptor D1 expression, helping mothers to be responsive to offspring during sleep.

items.title: Early lineage divergence segregates sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus
items.author: Guillermina López-Bendito
items.content: Sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus arise from two early-diverging lineages, with sensory neurons progressing through shared intermediate states, revealing how thalamic organization emerges during development.

items.title: Dysregulated cholesterol trafficking through ABCA1 drives neurodegeneration in Parkinson’s disease
items.author: Lei Cao
items.content: This study identifies ABCA1 as a driver of dysregulated cholesterol trafficking in Parkinson’s disease, showing that reducing ABCA1 in astrocytes and neurons decreases cholesterol accumulation, α-synuclein pathology and neurodegeneration in mice.
